question: Why was the change that caused INC-0412 made?
answer:
The change that caused INC-0412 was CHG-2291, which reduced the payments-db connection pool from 50 to 20 connections, and it was made because the Q1 capacity review recommended the reduction to allow a smaller database instance and save about 1,200 USD/month; sources disagree on when it was deployed: 09:05 [1] or 09:40 [2]. [1][2][3]

CHG-2291 is recorded as reducing the payments-db pool from 50 to 20 connections in both the incident timeline and the changelog. [1][2]

The change was recommended by the Q1 capacity review to permit a smaller database instance and save about 1,200 USD per month, and is tracked as CHG-2291. [3][4][2]

When checkout-api retried slow requests it published duplicate payment events that still cost database round trips and exhausted the reduced payments-db pool, causing ledger-worker consumer lag and delayed ledger writes; CHG-2291 was reverted during the incident (pool back to 50) and latency and lag returned toward normal. [5][6][1][2]
conflicts: The timeline record says CHG-2291 was deployed at 09:05 [1]; the changelog entry lists CHG-2291 at 09:40 [2].

question: What permanently fixed the cause of the February login outage?
answer:
The outage was caused by the auth-service TLS certificate expiring, and it was permanently fixed by automating TLS certificate renewal (CHG-2266) which renews certificates 30 days before expiry [1][2].

The incident report records that at 14:03 the auth-service TLS certificate expired, causing sign-ins to fail until a renewed certificate was installed manually at 14:25, and it states the certificate had been renewed by hand every year and the reminder was missed [1].

CHG-2266 is listed as the follow-up to INC-0398 and documents automated TLS certificate renewal for auth-service configured to renew 30 days before expiry, recorded on 9 Feb 2024 [2].
